long_description:
Overview

A rare opportunity to explore the attic at Old Government Buildings as we celebrate its 150th birthday.

Join our expert guide for a tour around the attic at Wellington's iconic Old Government Buildings.

You'll see some fascinating (and sometimes scandalous) historic graffiti, explore the old attic filing room, and view Old Government Buildings' clock, still wound every week by hand, from the inside.

Numbers are limited to ensure everyone enjoys themselves, so booking ahead ensures your place.

Please note that this tour requires you to step over struts and at times slip through tight spaces, therefore a reasonable standard of agility and fitness is required, along with appropriate clothing for a dusty attic.

Please meet your guide at the main entrance on Lambton Quay 10 minutes prior to your tour time.

Questions? Contact us at info@heritage.org.nz or (04) 494 8320.

This tour is part of a special event celebrating Old Government Buildings' 150th anniversary. Check our website for more events happening on the day.

name: Design a life you love
long_description:
Overview

Reconnect with what matters, discover your strengths and learn simple tools to design a life that feels truly yours.

Design a Life You Love




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




So often we go through life doing what is expected of us, without ever questioning why we are doing what we're doing. We chase promotions, juggle family life, and feel pulled in multiple directions at once. In this hands-on workshop, we will spend time reconnecting with what truly matters to us, reflect on our strengths and who we want to become, and use simple tools to decide where we spend our limited time and energy.

Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host, Ruth:

Ruth is a lawyer, author, entrepreneur, and still very much figuring it out step-mum. She holds a degree in psychology and a coaching qualification. After burning out at 29, Ruth went travelling and spent some time reconsidering her own life. Out of this she developed the VIP Mindset (Values, Identity, and Priorities). Having found a better balance for herself, Ruth is passionate about supporting people to live with intention, building lives that feel both meaningful and sustainable.

name: Ecstatic Dance: Into the Blue
long_description:
Overview

Let go and move freely through music, rhythm and intuitive dance in an evening of expression, connection and release.

Into the Blue: Ecstatic Dance




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




Step onto the dance floor, leave your shoes at the door and let the music guide you. Into the Blue is an evening of movement, freedom, expression and connection, inviting you to let go, move with the rhythm and simply be.

Ecstatic dance offers an opportunity to release stress, move through emotions, quiet the mind and reconnect with the body. Through intuitive movement and a carefully curated soundscape, you’ll be invited to explore presence, creativity and connection, both within yourself and with those around you.




Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!

Meet Divya, your host: 



Divya attended her first ecstatic dance a few years ago and will always remember the feeling of pure joy, freedom, and connection it brought. During that experience, she felt inspired to one day host her own ecstatic dance. Having explored the world of DJing, she was drawn to creating a more intentional space where people could express themselves through movement and music.

Over the past year, dance has become an important practice for helping her process emotions, stay present, and reconnect with herself. She is excited to share a carefully curated journey of music, blending uplifting rhythms, grounding beats, and at times bass-heavy sounds that invite people to move, explore, and enjoy the experience in their own way.

Turitea, Manawatū-Whanganui Region-Event Brite
name: The Big Think - Manawatū / Palmerston North
long_description:
Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

Read less

Our Leadership & Management Part 2 workshop will equip leaders and managers with the skills to build high performing and motivated teams.

long_description:
Overview

A magical adventure of courage, friendship and wonder. Join Gerda on her quest to rescue Kaj from the icy Snow Queen!

The Snow Queen

Adapted from Hans Christian Andersen’s tale by Jenny Wake

When Kaj is stolen away by the Snow Queen, his best friend Gerda sets out on a perilous journey to the North Pole, determined to find him and bring him home. Along the way she encounters a wicked band of grubby robbers, a garden of enchanted flowers, a prince and princess and their elegantly snobby courtiers, a feisty reindeer, some wise-cracking crows, a mysterious Arctic woman, an army of fierce snow warriors and, of course, the ice-cold Snow Queen.

The Snow Queen is about a young girl’s quest to rescue her friend. It is about the strength we each have inside us - the kind of courage we may not discover until we are most afraid. It is about the power of true friendship.




Performance details:

Date: Thursday 5 November

Matinee: 1.00pm

Evening Performance: 6.00pm

Venue: Little Theatre




Director: Allegra Canton

Production Manager: Sarah Malone

Musical Director: Jo Hodgson

Choreographer: Tayla Best




Adapted by Jenny Wake Calico Young People's Theatre

Produced by Chilton Saint James Primary School

Superman, The Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit, Indiana Jones, Star Wars, Narnia, Aliens, Harry Potter, Dr. Who and many more?

name: The Big Think - Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington
long_description:
Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.
